guidelineStrength: Five strong and 24 conditional recommendations, ten good-practice statements; evidence was insufficient for recommendations on 22 PICO questions.
title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign International Guidelines for the Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock in Children 2026
shortTitle: SSC 2026 children: reassess each bolus and recognize limited evidence
authors: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Pediatric Guideline Panel
summary: The pediatric update provides 61 statements, but only three recommendations have high- or moderate-certainty evidence. In settings with intensive care availability, it conditionally suggests up to 40–60 mL/kg during the first hour, using repeated small boluses and reassessment.
whyItMatters: Reassess perfusion and overload after every bolus and stop when shock resolves or overload develops. Do not apply the ICU-available fluid strategy to settings without intensive care support.
limitations: Most recommendations rely on low-certainty evidence or consensus. The guideline preceded PRoMPT BOLUS, which did not demonstrate better major kidney outcomes with balanced fluids.
population: Infants, children and adolescents with sepsis or septic shock.
intervention: Updated antimicrobial, fluid, hemodynamic and organ-support recommendations.
primaryEndpoint: GRADE-based recommendations rather than a single trial endpoint.
findings: For suspected septic shock, antimicrobials ideally within one hour: strong recommendation, very-low-certainty evidence.
With ICU availability, 10–20 mL/kg boluses up to 40–60 mL/kg in the first hour: conditional, low certainty.
Balanced crystalloid preference is conditional with very-low-certainty evidence; saline remains an alternative.
evidenceNotes: SCCM current recommendations and Springer abstract reviewed. Springer confirms March 23 publication, before the May issue. Complete guideline not reviewed; Pediatric Critical Care Medicine co-publication DOI 10.1097/PCC.0000000000003927 is the same guidance.
